papers.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
papers.abstract: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models. Today's dominant approach distills a bidirectional diffusion model into a causal few-step student, but existing pipelines make this conversion prohibitively expensive, requiring offline Probability Flow ODE} (PF-ODE) trajectories that cost tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of storage. We show it can be made dramatically more efficient. Pushing this efficiency to its extreme, we reduce trajectory supervision to a single sample, the strictest setting possible, and find that it causes severe quality collapse. We trace this to the teacher's trajectory geometry: the high-noise regime, governing semantic layout and motion, and the low-noise regime, governing fine texture exhibit fundamentally different curvature and optimization behavior, so a single monolithic student cannot jointly fit both, causing severe representation interference. Motivated by this, we propose Glance Forcing, a lightweight distillation framework that decouples the denoising trajectory into two complementary slow and fast experts, each guided by a tailored, stage-specific objective, while keeping the pretrained teacher entirely frozen. This decoupling further reveals a general mechanism underlying few-step distillation: PF-ODE distillation mainly straightens the few-step trajectory geometry, while the subsequent distribution-matching stage independently governs distributional quality. Using only one PF-ODE trajectory, Glance Forcing already surpasses the fully-trained state-of-the-art baseline, raising the VBench Total score from 84.04 to 84.22 while cutting trajectory-collection cost from thousands of GPU-hours to about one A100-GPU-hour, with markedly larger gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, and instruction-following, and consistent preference from human raters over strong baselines.
papers.summary_cn: 本文研究如何以极少的PF-ODE轨迹监督，将双向视频扩散模型高效蒸馏为可因果、自回归、少步生成的模型。作者发现，单样本监督本身足以建立少步轨迹的整体几何结构，但单一学生网络难以同时拟合高噪声阶段的布局与运动，以及低噪声阶段的纹理细节，原因在于两者的曲率和优化行为不同。为此提出Glance Forcing：使用双LoRA结构，将去噪过程划分为Slow专家和Fast专家，分别处理高噪声语义运动与低噪声细节，并引入时间频谱损失和空间高通损失。实验基于Wan2.1-1.3B的分块自回归生成，在单样本设置下显著降低轨迹收集成本；扩大训练预算后，VBench、动态程度、视觉奖励和指令遵循等指标进一步提升。消融实验验证了阶段解耦、时间频谱损失和空间高通损失的作用；此外，该方法也被用于将Wan2.1从50步压缩到8步或4步的双向扩散生成。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 分析PF-ODE蒸馏与分布匹配的作用，指出前者主要拉直少步去噪轨迹，后者主要改善生成分布质量，并证明单条轨迹可提供足够的轨迹几何监督。 2. 提出Glance Forcing双LoRA蒸馏框架，将去噪过程解耦为负责布局和运动的Slow专家，以及负责纹理和细节的Fast专家。 3. 为两个阶段设计专门目标：利用时间频谱损失抑制闪烁并保持运动动态，利用空间高通损失增强边缘和精细纹理。 4. 在极少轨迹监督下实现较高的数据与计算效率，并通过系统实验、消融实验和人类偏好评测验证方法有效性。 5. 展示该阶段感知优化策略不仅适用于自回归视频生成，也可用于双向扩散模型的采样步数压缩。
papers.relevance_cn: 本文与研究重点高度相关。它直接面向视频扩散模型到因果、自回归视频生成器的蒸馏，解决了长视频和实时生成中因果分块推理的训练成本问题。其分块自回归架构支持利用历史帧的KV缓存进行流式生成，适合实时视频合成和视频世界模型。双LoRA专家分别处理高噪声阶段的全局运动与语义布局、低噪声阶段的局部细节，属于针对视频时空生成过程的稀疏阶段建模和高效适配。单条PF-ODE轨迹将轨迹收集从数千GPU小时降低到约一个A100小时，直接涉及蒸馏、计算效率和训练数据压缩；4步或8步推理结果也与少步生成和实时生成相关。论文没有重点研究闭环动作条件控制或交互式世界模型中的策略反馈，但其因果生成和流式自回归机制可作为此类系统的视频预测模块。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文显示，单样本ODE初始化对样本特征较敏感：高运动强度、特定领域和复杂内容会导致更明显的性能下降；单样本训练的效果取决于样本选择。虽然DMD能够在一定程度上恢复质量，但不同样本设置下的结果仍有差异。方法的实验主要基于Wan2.1-1.3B、特定分辨率和81帧分块生成，跨模型、分辨率、视频长度及更复杂场景的泛化能力未被充分验证。实时性结果是在单张H100 GPU上、且不计VAE时间的条件下测量，实际端到端延迟可能更高。论文主要评估离线生成质量和效率，没有充分验证动作条件控制、闭环交互、长期世界模型稳定性或误差累积。论文未明确说明在极长视频、连续流式运行或更大规模模型上的性能上限。
papers.abstract_cn: 自回归生成是实时、因果视频合成的基础，也是视频世界模型的核心。当前主流方法将双向扩散模型蒸馏为因果少步学生模型，但现有流程需要离线概率流常微分方程（PF-ODE）轨迹，成本高得难以承受，需消耗数万GPU小时和数TB存储。我们证明，这一过程可以大幅提高效率。为将效率推向极致，我们将轨迹监督减少到单个样本这一最严格的设置，并发现这会导致严重的质量崩溃。我们追溯其原因发现，教师模型的轨迹几何存在明显差异：负责语义布局和运动的高噪声阶段，与负责精细纹理的低噪声阶段具有根本不同的曲率和优化行为，因此单一的整体学生模型无法同时拟合二者，导致严重的表示干扰。基于这一观察，我们提出Glance Forcing，一种轻量级蒸馏框架，将去噪轨迹解耦为互补的慢速专家和快速专家，并分别采用针对阶段特点设计的目标函数，同时完全冻结预训练教师模型。这种解耦进一步揭示了少步蒸馏背后的一般机制：PF-ODE蒸馏主要负责拉直少步轨迹的几何结构，而后续的分布匹配阶段则独立决定分布质量。仅使用一条PF-ODE轨迹，Glance Forcing就已经超过了经过完整训练的先进基线，将VBench总分从84.04提高到84.22，同时将轨迹收集成本从数千GPU小时降至约一个A100 GPU小时；在动态程度、VisionReward和指令遵循方面取得了更显著的提升，并且在人类评测者中持续获得相对于强基线的偏好。

papers.title: TRAC: Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video generation enables scalable long-video synthesis by sequentially generating fixed-length chunks, but incurs substantial computational cost from repeated denoising and attention over growing historical contexts. Recent cache reuse methods exploit temporal redundancy to reduce this cost, yet are mainly designed for single-trajectory generation, making them less suitable for sequentially coupled AR trajectories where approximation errors can accumulate and propagate across chunks. To address this challenge, we propose TRAC, a Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction framework for efficient and robust AR video generation. TRAC integrates three complementary components: (1) Robust Cumulative Scheduling (RCS), which selects cache reuse schedules by accounting for cumulative rollout errors and their variation across chunks and prompts; (2) Autoregressive Trajectory-aware Guidance Scheduling (ATGS), which coordinates classifier-free guidance refreshes along the global AR trajectory; and (3) Spectral Structure Correction (SSC), which adaptively restores low-frequency structural information to mitigate long-term error accumulation. By combining these innovations, TRAC substantially improves the efficiency-quality trade-off of AR video generation. For example, on VBench with SkyReels-V2, it achieves a 6.03x speedup over the vanilla model with only ~0.6% VBench score degradation, while consistently outperforming existing AR acceleration methods in both latency and generation quality. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/yolosjxhhhhhh/trac.
papers.summary_cn: 本文提出一种无需训练的TRAC框架，用于加速由连续视频块组成的自回归长视频生成。针对缓存复用误差沿AR轨迹累积、CFG计算开销高以及长期低频结构漂移三个问题，TRAC分别采用RCS、ATGS和SSC进行风险感知的缓存调度、全局CFG刷新调度和自适应低频结构校正。在SkyReels-V2上，TRAC达到6.03倍加速，VBench得分为82.44，相比原始模型仅下降约0.6%；在FramePack-F1上达到1.668倍加速，并保持接近原始模型的总体质量。
papers.contribution_cn: 提出面向序列耦合AR生成轨迹的TRAC训练免费加速框架；提出RCS，通过跨视频块和提示词的稳健统计、累积 rollout 误差、尾部风险及终点误差来优化缓存调度，并为首个视频块分配更密集的计算；提出ATGS，将CFG残差刷新建模为全局AR路径上的预算调度问题，在高误差位置刷新、其他位置复用；提出SSC，利用首个视频块的低频结构作为参考，并依据局部运动强度自适应注入校正，从而缓解长期结构漂移；在SkyReels-V2和FramePack-F1上验证了效率与生成质量的提升。
papers.relevance_cn: 与研究重点高度相关。该工作直接面向自回归、因果式的长视频生成，核心目标是降低连续块式生成中的重复去噪、增长历史上下文注意力和CFG开销。RCS和ATGS分别涉及跨轨迹缓存复用与全局引导调度，SSC则通过低频结构保持改善长时一致性。其结果表明，在SkyReels-V2上可实现6.03倍推理加速，在FramePack-F1上可实现1.668倍加速；方法为训练免费，并明确指出可与量化、蒸馏和稀疏注意力等实时生成技术结合。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，TRAC仅在两个自回归视频骨干模型上进行了验证，能否推广到新兴AR视频模型仍是开放问题；验证更广泛模型需要目前无法承担的大量计算资源。TRAC尚未与量化、蒸馏、稀疏注意力等互补加速技术结合，因此联合方案的效果尚未评估。论文还依赖校准阶段对提示词、视频块和调度进行误差统计，并将调度固定用于推理；不同数据分布、模型或运行条件下的校准成本和泛化表现未作充分说明。
papers.abstract_cn: 自回归（AR）视频生成通过依次生成固定长度的视频块，实现了可扩展的长视频合成，但由于需要重复去噪并对不断增长的历史上下文执行注意力计算，因此计算成本很高。近期的缓存复用方法利用时间冗余来降低这一成本，但主要针对单轨迹生成设计，因此不太适用于具有序列耦合关系的AR轨迹；在后者中，近似误差可能跨视频块累积并传播。为应对这一挑战，我们提出TRAC（Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction，轨迹感知复用与自适应校正）框架，以实现高效且稳健的AR视频生成。TRAC包含三个互补组件：（1）稳健累积调度（RCS），通过考虑累积的 rollout 误差及其在不同视频块和提示词之间的变化来选择缓存复用调度；（2）自回归轨迹感知引导调度（ATGS），沿全局AR轨迹协调无分类器引导的刷新；（3）谱结构校正（SSC），自适应地恢复低频结构信息，以减轻长期误差累积。通过结合这些创新，TRAC显著改善了AR视频生成的效率—质量权衡。例如，在使用SkyReels-V2的VBench上，与原始模型相比，它实现了6.03倍加速，而VBench得分仅下降约0.6%；同时，在延迟和生成质量方面始终优于现有AR加速方法。代码已公开于https://github.com/yolosjxhhhhhh/trac。

papers.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient
papers.abstract: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry. Velox represents historical blocks as camera frustum slabs with depth intervals and obtains current-block depth through recency-priority multiwarp. For well-covered regions, frustum slab overlap softly modulates each layer's model-derived block importance. Uncovered regions retain the model-derived route without geometric bias. The fixed token-block granularity matches FlashAttention-style tiled execution and reduces the attention term that grows with rollout length. Frustum slab construction runs asynchronously with denoising on the same H200. At chunk 48, Velox accelerates attention by $4.36\times$ and denoising by $2.43\times$. On the full 158-case WBench navigation split, it remains within 0.15 API-free average points of dense LingBot-Fast-Cam. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/velox/ for more details.
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对长时视频世界模型中 KV 缓存随生成历史增长、导致后续分块越来越慢的问题，提出无需训练的 Velox 推理路由器。它把历史视觉记忆压缩表示为带深度区间的相机视锥体 slab，通过多重变形估计当前块深度，并以世界坐标系中的 slab 重叠作为几何先验，结合每个 Transformer 层自身的注意力重要性，为当前区域选择有限的历史 KV 块。对几何覆盖不足的区域，系统回退到模型路由；同时保留前一分块、全局 Gilbert 邻域和参考帧等局部连续性保护机制。Velox 使用块稀疏注意力、全局对齐的 Gilbert KV 布局，并在 H200 上异步构建几何记忆。在 48 分块 rollout 的末端，注意力和去噪分别获得 4.36 倍和 2.43 倍加速；在 158 个 WBench 导航案例上，质量接近稠密注意力，并略微提升整体平均分。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 Velox，一种无需训练的区域级注意力路由框架，利用视锥体 slab 对应关系降低分块视频世界模型不断增长的 KV 注意力开销。2. 提出软几何融合规则，以 OBB 视锥体 slab 重叠调制各层模型推导的块重要性，同时对几何覆盖不足的区域保留无偏的模型路由回退。3. 在实现层面结合全局对齐的 Gilbert KV 存储、原生索引块稀疏注意力内核，以及与去噪并行的异步视锥体 slab 构建，在第 48 个分块达到 4.36 倍注意力加速和 2.43 倍去噪加速。4. 通过 WBench 导航评测、缩放实验、几何与模型重要性一致性分析及定性 rollout 对比，验证其在降低延迟的同时维持长时空间一致性的能力。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关：它直接面向动作和相机控制的视频世界模型及闭环式长时视觉 rollout，解决长视频生成中的历史记忆管理和响应速度问题。方法属于推理阶段的稀疏注意力与 KV 缓存复用，通过空间几何对应关系进行区域级上下文路由，而不是让每个当前区域访问全部历史。固定块路由使注意力开销不再随历史长度线性增长，并在单张 H200 上异步执行几何处理，因而与实时生成、长视频生成、缓存复用和高效视频扩散密切相关。它保持预训练生成器和条件接口不变，也体现了无需再训练即可进行生成加速的路线。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文的实验主要基于 LingBot-Fast-Cam 推理栈、单张 H200 和 158 个 WBench 导航案例，跨模型、硬件和任务的泛化能力未得到充分验证。方法依赖深度、置信度、掩码和相机位姿等流式几何信息；深度空洞、遮挡、错误重建或陈旧的变形深度可能降低路由可靠性。视锥体 slab 状态通常存在两分块的新鲜度延迟，且几何构建与去噪共享同一块 GPU，其他硬件条件下的实际收益可能不同。Velox 使用固定的路由预算和多个校准超参数，可能在不同场景、运动模式或覆盖率下需要重新调整。论文报告了总体质量和部分定性案例，但未明确说明更长于 48 个分块、极端快速相机运动、复杂动态物体或真实交互闭环中的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 视频世界模型将动作和相机运动转化为长时视觉 rollout，使视频成为交互式模拟的自然接口。这类交互要求生成具有响应性，但连贯的 rollout 必须保留已生成内容的视觉记忆。分块视频扩散模型通常将这些上下文保存在不断增长的 KV 缓存中，因此后续分块会逐渐变慢。为解决这一瓶颈，我们提出 Velox：一种无需训练的注意力路由器，利用流式几何中的视锥体 slab 对应关系进行区域级上下文选择。Velox 将历史块表示为带有深度区间的相机视锥体 slab，并通过基于新近性的多重变形获取当前块的深度。对于覆盖良好的区域，视锥体 slab 的重叠程度会对模型在各层推导出的块重要性进行软调制；未覆盖区域则保留模型推导的路由，不施加几何偏置。固定的 token 块粒度与 FlashAttention 风格的分块执行相匹配，从而降低随 rollout 长度增长的注意力开销。视锥体 slab 的构建与去噪过程在同一块 H200 上异步运行。在第 48 个分块处，Velox 将注意力加速 4.36 倍，将去噪加速 2.43 倍。在完整的 158 个案例 WBench 导航划分上，其无 API 平均分与稠密 LingBot-Fast-Cam 相差不超过 0.15 分。更多细节请参见项目主页 https://velox-world.com/velox/。

papers.title: ORD-WM: Learning Object-Centric Rigid Dynamics for 3D World Modeling in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: World models provide robots with a predictive mechanism for reasoning about how actions change object states in manipulation tasks. However, existing image-based and dense 3D world models do not explicitly impose object-level rigid motion, leaving rigid-object geometry preservation to be learned implicitly and making multi-step rollouts susceptible to shape drift or object-level motion inconsistency. To address this, we propose ORD-WM, a 3D world model that learns object-centric rigid dynamics for robotic manipulation. ORD-WM learns a vector-neuron variational autoencoder supervised by signed distance fields, which encodes each object point cloud as a geometry-aware latent representation composed of 3D vector features, and uses an action-conditioned dynamics model to predict object-wise SE(3) motion increments. Rather than generating unconstrained next latent states, ORD-WM analytically applies predicted object-wise rigid transformations to the current latent states, separating persistent object geometry from pose changes. Experiments show that ORD-WM enables stable, geometry-preserving multi-step prediction and supports efficient real-time replanning for closed-loop model predictive control in simulated and real-world manipulation scenarios.
papers.summary_cn: World models provide robots with a predictive mechanism for reasoning about how actions change object states in manipulation tasks.
papers.contribution_cn: To address this, we propose ORD-WM, a 3D world model that learns object-centric rigid dynamics for robotic manipulation.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model, efficient generation；关键词：world model, action-conditioned, closed-loop, real-time, efficient
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We find this uniform computation is often unnecessary: many tokens already closely match their eventual full-step outputs in the initial steps, while others require refinement until the end. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early. Once accepted, a token is frozen as its final output and undergoes no further denoising, while its cached keys and values remain available as context for the remaining tokens. We explore two alternative verifier designs: a training-free one based on similarity to clean content and stability across steps, and a learned one that reads the frozen generator's intermediate features to estimate each token's remaining gap to its full-step output. Across short-video, long-video, and world generation, Speculative Forcing preserves the quality of full-step sampling while substantially reducing computation. On LongLive, it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5x faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps. On Lingbot-World 2.0, where camera motion continually changes the visible content, it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token and runs 1.35x faster at 24.5 fps.
papers.summary_cn: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early.

papers.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.

papers.title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
papers.abstract: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. We introduce a paradigm that decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state. The abstract state keeps track of the entities' changes as the world evolves, and is used to condition the visual state, which represents the current view. We propose StateCraft, a novel architecture that pairs a language model with a video diffusion model to evolve the dynamic world. We evaluate our approach on generative interfaces, which pose a substantial challenge because a single action may change parts of the state that are not currently visible. To support training and evaluation, we develop a data collection pipeline that produces informative, densely annotated trajectories at scale without human or agent supervision, together with a benchmark measuring generation quality, memory, and controllability. On this benchmark, our approach improves surpasses the state-of-the-art baselines. We demonstrate that StateCraft maintains high self-consistency and strong generation quality over long trajectories. Because the abstract state is explicit, it can be edited directly, and generation follows edits to states never observed in the data. Finally, a proof-of-concept 3D experiment, in which actions change the illumination of an unobserved room, shows that the paradigm can also be applied to spatial environments. Project page: https://insait-institute.github.io/StateCraft/.

papers.title: Momentum: Persistent Dynamics for Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models must capture how a scene evolves beyond the current camera view to generate consistent observations when its content reappears. Existing approaches rely on observation history, static point clouds, or image caches constructed from past frames. These representations are often expensive and, more importantly, cannot update dynamic scene content outside the field of view: generated vehicles and pedestrians may be forgotten after leaving the field of view or reappear in physically inaccurate states. We represent an evolving scene through synchronized videos from reference-camera rigs, each comprising eight cameras that jointly cover the surrounding scene. We connect these rigs in a graph and propagate video generation between neighboring rigs to coordinate scene dynamics across locations and time. We introduce Momentum, a two-stage pipeline: WorldUpdate jointly generates reference-camera videos as a shared memory of scene dynamics, and WorldInteract grounds camera-controlled video generation in this evolving memory, allowing moving content to remain represented outside the target view and reappear consistently. To support training and evaluation, we develop a CARLA pipeline that captures synchronized videos from reference camera rigs and a moving target camera, together with an evaluation framework measuring consistency within the generated world state and the target observations.Experiments on generated street scenes show that grounding target videos in scene dynamics generated by Momentum improves dynamic scene consistency by 126.2% in unseen scenes over static image conditioning, while also improving visual fidelity. Our models and source code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
papers.abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. For generated-content persistence, we compare revisits to regions absent from the input image with their first generated observations to test whether models preserve what they create. For 3D self-consistency, cross-view depth and feature correspondence, regional scale agreement, and held-out Gaussian rendering test whether generated views describe the same 3D scene. Minute-long exploration and revisits further test long-term consistency. Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.

papers.title: RepForcing: Representation-Space Initialization for Autoregressive Video Distillation
papers.abstract: Distilling pretrained video diffusion models into few-step autoregressive (AR) generators typically combines student initialization with distribution matching distillation (DMD). An intermediate AR teacher can provide causally compatible targets for ODE initialization. However, causally compatible targets alone do not ensure high-quality generation under a short sampling schedule. We analyze the posterior-mean predictions favored by direct latent regression and empirically find that causal ODE initialization alleviates blur but still leaves fine detail unresolved. To address this limitation, we propose Representation Forcing, which learns few-step causal initialization through representation-space supervision rather than intermediate-teacher trajectory regression. The student is trained with teacher forcing by comparing clean predictions and training targets through normalized features of a frozen video diffusion transformer. This phase reuses the synthetic videos generated by a bidirectional model for AR teacher training and replaces both teacher training and causal ODE distillation, without generating additional causal ODE trajectories. The subsequent asymmetric DMD procedure remains unchanged. Empirical results show that, at four sampling steps, RepForcing better preserves generation quality than intermediate-teacher-based initialization before DMD. After DMD, our four-step chunk-wise model improves VBench Total from 84.04 to 84.66 (+0.62 points) and VisionReward from 6.326 to 10.074 (+59.25%) over the reported causal-ODE-based baseline.
